content.intro: Learn why is django used? through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Why Is Django Used? matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines why is django used? as part of introduction to django. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Rapid application development; Built-in administrative interface; Database-driven applications; Security and maintainability; Convention-based development. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Rapid application development
items.text: An API contract specifies resources, methods, body validation, authentication, permissions, status codes, pagination, versioning and error formats. JSON transport alone does not make an API safe or complete.

items.title: Built-in administrative interface
items.text: For Built-in administrative interface, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: Database-driven applications
items.text: Database-driven applications affects persistence and data correctness. Keep invariants in validation and database constraints where appropriate, inspect generated SQL/migrations, and test both expected data and error/rollback behavior.

items.title: Security and maintainability
items.text: Security and maintainability is a server-side responsibility where applicable. Define who may perform the action and on which object, validate untrusted input, test denied cases, and document sensitive-data handling.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Change one input or configuration choice related to Rapid application development. Write down the expected outcome, test one normal case and one invalid or boundary case, then record what changed. Do not add real credentials or sensitive production data.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
